loop_start.reason: Compiler loops start from CodeWiki source refs; agents may refresh context when chat is noisy, stale, or token-heavy.

validation.reason: Fresh validation is preferred; policy may require it for high-risk semantic gates.

next_loop.reason: The next compiler loop should start from CodeWiki source refs; the agent may refresh context when useful.

requirements.text: Runtime owns generic context-boundary dispatch for subagents, compaction, fresh gate evaluation, parallel continuation, and future session spawning.

Spawned or compacted sessions start from a trace pointer or focused graph lens plus scoped source refs, expected output, constraints, budgets, blockers, artifact status, and content-evidence requirements.
Role is not a canonical scheduling, gate, or policy axis; existing role fields are compatibility labels only until migrated.

summary: Accept runtime-owned role-free context session dispatch and high-signal source-backed context packet contract.

decision_table.title: Accept runtime-owned role-free context session dispatch and high-signal source-backed context packet contract.

rows.question: RCS-001-RUNTIME-OWNS-SPAWN

state_delta.current: Session spawning is discussed through worker/validator/publication compatibility labels and current agency planning surfaces can imply role-specific dispatch paths.
state_delta.desired: Runtime owns one generic subagent/session dispatch mechanism for any source-backed context boundary, regardless of decision/planning/implementation timing.

rows.proposed_change: Runtime owns one generic subagent/session dispatch mechanism for any source-backed context boundary, regardless of decision/planning/implementation timing.
rows.rationale: Spawning is execution coordination, not semantic loop ownership. One runtime mechanism can serve planning workers, gate review, context-bloat refresh, parallel work, and future agent sessions without adding loop roots.

options.label: Let each loop own its own session-spawn mechanism.

rows.expected_outcome: Runtime owns one generic subagent/session dispatch mechanism for any source-backed context boundary, regardless of decision/planning/implementation timing.

rows.question: RCS-002-TRACE-REFS-NOT-CHAT

state_delta.current: Fresh validation and compaction can be framed as role-bound sessions or rely on broad context packets that risk noisy chat/history carryover.
state_delta.desired: Spawned or compacted sessions start from a high-signal trace pointer, graph lens, scoped source refs, expected output, constraints, and content-evidence requirements; they do not rely on chat history or graph dumps.

rows.proposed_change: Spawned or compacted sessions start from a high-signal trace pointer, graph lens, scoped source refs, expected output, constraints, and content-evidence requirements; they do not rely on chat history or graph dumps.
rows.rationale: CodeWiki truth lives in KB/trace/source refs and graph state. Trace-head plus source refs gives token-efficient continuation while preserving source-backed verification.

options.label: Send full graph/context dump to subagents.
Use chat compaction summaries as primary continuation memory.

rows.expected_outcome: Spawned or compacted sessions start from a high-signal trace pointer, graph lens, scoped source refs, expected output, constraints, and content-evidence requirements; they do not rely on chat history or graph dumps.

rows.question: RCS-003-NO-CANONICAL-ROLES

state_delta.current: Runtime and gateway isolation metadata currently includes role-like fields, and discussion used validator/worker labels as if they were core policy concepts.
state_delta.desired: Do not make role a canonical scheduling, gate, or policy axis. If compatibility fields remain, treat them as optional labels only; runtime dispatch is driven by reason, trace scope, expected output, constraints, budgets, and source refs.

rows.proposed_change: Do not make role a canonical scheduling, gate, or policy axis. If compatibility fields remain, treat them as optional labels only; runtime dispatch is driven by reason, trace scope, expected output, constraints, budgets, and source refs.
rows.rationale: Role labels are not in the desired mental model and constrain future trace-cycle behavior. Sessions may be spawned for context bloat, review, repair, or continuation at arbitrary points in the cycle.

options.label: Keep roles as required dispatch field.
Create fixed role enum for validator/builder/planner/publisher.

rows.expected_outcome: Do not make role a canonical scheduling, gate, or policy axis. If compatibility fields remain, treat them as optional labels only; runtime dispatch is driven by reason, trace scope, expected output, constraints, budgets, and source refs.

accepted_decisions.summary: Runtime, not individual loops or gates, owns session spawning and context-boundary mechanics.
Trace/source-ref packets, not chat history or graph dumps, are the continuation substrate.
Roles are removed from the canonical mental model and retained only as migration compatibility labels.

row_to_kb_mappings.evidence: Runtime, agency, gateway, and lexicon now state that runtime owns generic role-free context-boundary dispatch for subagents, compaction, gates, and future session spawning.
Docs define Source-backed context packet and graph-lens/trace-pointer behavior, explicitly excluding full chat history and graph dumps.
Lexicon adds role as temporary compatibility term; runtime/agency/gateway docs say role labels are compatibility metadata only, not scheduling, policy, or gate criteria.
row_to_kb_mappings.no_diagram_impact: Role removal is vocabulary/policy semantics already covered by component/data-model updates for dispatch packet shape; no additional diagram node is needed.

system_impact: Runtime dispatch becomes generic and role-free.
Context-bloat, fresh gate, parallel work, review, and replacement sessions use one context-boundary mechanism.
Source-backed context packets become the high-signal continuation contract.
Gateway freshness is context-boundary/content-evidence based, not validator-role based.
Legacy role fields are compatibility labels only.
propagation.no_product_impact: This changes internal system architecture vocabulary and workflow contracts; no user-facing product UI behavior changes yet.

downstream_planning_questions: Plan executable work to implement generic runtime context-boundary dispatch without canonical role labels.
Plan source/schema migration or compatibility facade for existing role fields and worktree paths.
Plan high-signal Source-backed context packet shape from trace pointer, graph lens, source refs, expected output, constraints, and content evidence.
Reconcile with existing context-bloat auto-refresh decision rows and TASK-115 runtime/gateway contracts.
assumptions: Current source still contains compatibility role fields and role-worktree wording; migration can be planned separately without blocking semantic acceptance.
Existing TASK-115 implementation remains valid but should route follow-up runtime/session dispatch changes through planning.
non_goals: Do not implement source changes in the decision loop.
Do not remove compatibility role fields immediately.
Do not create validation or publish loop roots.
